stimuli.text: Researchers want to investigate whether a new fertilizer increases tomato yield. They have 40 garden plots available.

Random samples of 15 were taken from two groups. The values of commute time (minutes) are:

**City A:** 10, 11, 13, 14, 14, 15, 18, 21, 21, 22, 23, 24, 26, 27, 30

**City B:** 19, 20, 21, 24, 26, 26, 30, 30, 32, 36, 36, 42, 44, 44, 74
In a randomized experiment on a new study strategy, 138 of 230 students using the new strategy passed a test, compared with 103 of 250 students using the usual strategy.

Data were collected on age of car (years) (x) and price (thousands of dollars) (y) for a sample of used cars. A scatterplot shows a linear pattern, and the residual plot shows no pattern. Computer output for the least-squares regression is shown.

```text
Predictor   Coef      SE Coef
Constant    25.3
x           -1.2
S = 2.2    R-Sq = 62.0%
```

questions.stem: The data are: 10, 13, 17, 20, 20, 22, 23, 29, 29, 32, 65. Using the 1.5 × IQR rule, which statement is correct?

options.text: There are no outliers because every value is within 2 standard deviations of the mean

options.text: Q1 = 17, Q3 = 29; values above 47 are outliers, so 65 is an outlier
options.why: Correct. IQR = 12; upper fence = Q3 + 1.5·IQR = 47.

options.text: Q1 = 17, Q3 = 29; values above 41 are outliers, so 65 is an outlier
options.why: The fence uses 1.5 × IQR, not 1 × IQR.

options.text: Q1 = 17, Q3 = 29; values above 40 are outliers
options.why: Add 1.5·IQR to Q3, not to the median.

questions.stem: The correlation between temperature and ice cream sales is r = -0.7. Which is a correct interpretation of r²?

options.text: About 49% of the predictions are correct
options.why: r² is about variation explained, not accuracy of individual predictions.

options.text: Temperature causes 49% of ice cream sales
options.why: Regression does not establish causation.

options.text: About 70% of the variation in ice cream sales is accounted for by the model
options.why: Square r.

options.text: About 49% of the variation in ice cream sales is accounted for by the linear model relating ice cream sales to temperature
options.why: Correct. r² is the proportion of variation in y explained by the linear model.

questions.stem: P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.24. What is P(A or B), and are A and B independent?

options.why: Compare P(A and B) with P(A)·P(B) = 0.24.
Subtract P(A and B) so the overlap is not counted twice.
Correct. P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B); independent if P(A and B) = P(A)P(B) = 0.24.
P(A and B) is not 0, so they are not mutually exclusive.

Correct. 1 − P(none fail) = 1 − (1 − p)^n.

questions.stem: In a randomized experiment, 75 of 250 subjects improved with treatment 1 and 133 of 290 improved with treatment 2. For a test of H₀: p₁ − p₂ = 0, what is the test statistic?

options.why: Use (1/n₁ + 1/n₂).
The test uses the pooled proportion, because H₀ assumes p₁ = p₂.
Divide the difference by its standard error.

parts.prompt: Write an investigative question for this study, and identify the explanatory and response variables.

rubric.criterion: A clear investigative question that names the population or units and the variables.
rubric.example: "Does the new fertilizer lead to a better total weight of tomatoes harvested than the standard fertilizer for units like these?"
Explanatory: treatment (the new fertilizer vs the standard fertilizer). Response: total weight of tomatoes harvested.

parts.prompt: Explain why an experiment, rather than an observational study, should be used to answer the question.

rubric.criterion: Only random assignment allows a cause-and-effect conclusion; an observational study could be confounded.
rubric.example: Units that choose a treatment may differ in other ways that affect the response.

parts.prompt: Describe how to randomly assign the 40 units to the two treatments in a completely randomized design.

rubric.example: Number units 1–40; use a random number generator to select 20 different numbers.
Those 20 receive the new fertilizer; the remaining 20 receive the standard fertilizer.

parts.prompt: The researchers consider blocking by sun exposure (full sun or partial shade). Explain how blocking would be carried out and why it could improve the experiment.

rubric.criterion: Form blocks and randomize within each block.
rubric.example: Separate units into the blocks, then randomly assign half of each block to each treatment.

rubric.criterion: Benefit: reduces variability in the response due to the blocking variable, making a treatment effect easier to detect.
rubric.example: Accounts for differences caused by sun exposure.

parts.prompt: Find the five-number summary for each group.
Use the 1.5 × IQR rule to determine whether City B has any outliers. Show your work.

rubric.example: IQR = 18; upper fence = 42 + 1.5(18) = 69. Outlier(s): 74.

parts.prompt: Compare the distributions of the two groups (shape, center and variability) in context.

rubric.example: The median for City B (30) is greater than for City A (21).
City B is more variable (IQR 18 vs 10).

rubric.criterion: Comments on shape or unusual features.
rubric.example: City B has a high outlier, suggesting right skew.

parts.prompt: Which measure of center is more appropriate for City B, the mean or the median? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Median, because it is resistant to the outlier or skew.
rubric.example: Mean 33.6 is pulled toward the high value; median 30 is not.

parts.prompt: State hypotheses to test whether the new strategy leads to a higher pass rate.

rubric.example: H₀: p₁ − p₂ = 0; Hₐ: p₁ − p₂ > 0, where p₁ and p₂ are the true pass rates with the new and usual strategies.

parts.prompt: Name the procedure and check the conditions.

rubric.criterion: Two-sample z test; random assignment; large counts with the pooled proportion.

parts.prompt: Calculate the test statistic and p-value.
State a conclusion in context at α = 0.05, including what kind of conclusion the design allows.

rubric.criterion: Correct decision; causal language justified by random assignment.
rubric.example: Reject H₀: convincing evidence that the new strategy causes a higher pass rate (random assignment).

parts.prompt: Write the equation of the least-squares regression line, defining the variables.

rubric.example: ŷ = 25.3 − 1.2x, where ŷ is predicted price (thousands of dollars) and x is age of car (years).

parts.prompt: Interpret the slope and the value of R-Sq in context.

rubric.example: For each additional unit of age of car (years), the predicted price (thousands of dollars) decreases by about 1.2.
About 62.0% of the variation in price (thousands of dollars) is accounted for by the linear model with age of car (years).

parts.prompt: One observation has x = 12 and y = 13.6. Calculate and interpret its residual. Also find the correlation r.

rubric.example: ŷ = 10.9; residual = 13.6 − 10.9 = 2.7: the actual value is above the prediction.

parts.prompt: The data come from a convenience sample. Explain how this affects the conclusions and describe a better data collection method.

rubric.criterion: Results may not generalize to the population; a random sample would allow generalization.
rubric.example: Take a simple random sample of used cars from the population of interest. Observational data also cannot show causation.
